steps.what: Assess equipment condition and appropriate preventive or general maintenance needs
Recommend or develop an appropriate maintenance approach within authorised procedures
Perform authorised preventive maintenance such as cleaning lubrication or filter replacement

tasks.design: Keep assessment, recommendations and physical maintenance with the qualified mechanic. Existing {DOCS} procedures support the work, but no generic generated procedure replaces equipment-specific judgement or handling.
tasks.previous_blocker: Maintenance depends on equipment condition and authorised physical work.
tasks.enabler_now: No validated replacement for those actions is established in this design.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising when routine maintenance is inappropriate or insufficient.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing condition differences and knowing when to escalate.
tasks.altitude: No change to maintenance responsibility or authority.

reach.task: Review equipment conditions requiring a changed maintenance approach
reach.learn: Which deviations exceed routine authorised work

evidence.claim: The design retains assessment and physical maintenance without a software labour-saving claim.

assumptions: Boundary is maintenance assessment/recommendation/performance, excluding separate recordkeeping and formal procedure authoring.
s1 produces observed needs through retained inspection; no structured maintenance decision feed is assumed.
Existing manufacturer recommendations and authorised procedures are unchanged upstream inputs.
No new system or ongoing upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Equipment types and local authorised maintenance scope
research_questions: Is repeated formal procedure drafting an actual separate burden?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+15+50=100. Assessment, recommendations and physical maintenance retain all time; new upkeep is zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep repair replacement and malfunction records

steps.what: Capture repair facts time parts faults and assessed causes at the job
Copy repairs replacements and malfunction causes into equipment repair history
Check repair history entry and save confirmed facts with unresolved causes explicit

tasks.design: Configure one service capture form in {OTHER} maintenance management software and derive the draft equipment-history entry from those fields. The mechanic still records the facts and checks the exact history entry; unknown causes remain unknown rather than being inferred.
tasks.previous_blocker: Already captured repair facts are recopied into a separate asset history.
tasks.enabler_now: Native work-order and asset-history records can share captured fields.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing a confirmed cause from a symptom or provisional explanation.
tasks.human_edge: Recording uncertainty faithfully so future repairs are not misled.
tasks.altitude: Less history recopying; source capture and record accountability stay with the mechanic.

reach.task: Use checked repair history to investigate repeat faults
reach.learn: Which evidence supports a cause rather than a symptom

evidence.claim: Ultimo EAM provides preventive plans, repair history and mobile work orders, supporting native record reuse.
Eliminating separate history recopying and the stated time split are unmeasured model assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary is mechanic repair-history recording, excluding repair execution and engineering diagnosis.

The mechanic produces asset ID, work-order ID, date, time, part/quantity, work performed, fault description, cause assessment and uncertainty in retained s1 time; all structured form entry is counted there.
s1 is exactly the same fact-capture action as in the work-order reporting task and carries the same shared ID; allocate it once before any team or role aggregation.

s2 copies explicit fields only and does not invent a fault/cause code. Missing asset matches or unsupported forms fall back to manual recording within retained capture/checking time; sustained fallback removes the projected saving.
Test native asset-history configuration first. Existing automatic history generation earns no new saving.
s3 retains exact-version verification and saving. Changed source facts invalidate the previous approval.
unknowns: Existing automatic history generation and true separate recopying burden
research_questions: Does one captured service record populate history without extra coding or reduced source verification?

already_counted.description: History check, exceptions and save approval in s3

incremental.description: Maintain history mappings and inspect asset-link failures

approvals.approved_version: Exact asset/work-order IDs, repair/replacement fields, time, fault description, cause assessment and uncertainty in the history entry; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Standalone task B=100, R=40+0+20=60; gross 40 minus 1 upkeep gives net 39. High requires genuine separate history recopying; low covers already-automatic history or manual asset-match fallback. Shared capture cannot be added twice with work-order reporting.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record and report service work orders

steps.what: Capture repair facts time parts faults and assessed causes at the job
Record time materials faults deficiencies and unusual occurrences on work orders
Check completed work order and report unresolved deficiencies through the existing route

tasks.design: Configure the mobile work order in {OTHER} maintenance management software to reuse the captured facts and assigned job details. The mechanic retains capture, exception descriptions and the final report check; no model decides a fault code or closes an unresolved deficiency.
tasks.previous_blocker: Field facts are rewritten into work-order sections after service.
tasks.enabler_now: Native mobile records can reuse job references and captured entries.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual occurrences that need a clear factual description and prompt escalation.
tasks.human_edge: Making uncertainty and incomplete work visible to the next responsible person.
tasks.altitude: Less work-order rewriting; reporting responsibility remains unchanged.

evidence.claim: OutSmart provides digital work orders for installers, supporting testing native work-order configuration.
The proposed time reduction is model knowledge, not a measured HVAC reporting result.

assumptions: Boundary is mechanic recording and reporting; repair execution, planning and billing remain outside and unchanged.

The mechanic produces asset/job identifiers, date, time, parts/quantity, work facts, faults, assessed causes and uncertainty in retained s1 time. Deficiencies and unusual occurrences are described in retained s2 time.
s1 is the same fact-capture action as in repair-history recording; its stable shared ID requires ownership resolution before roll-up.
The existing planner produces assigned job details through unchanged planning. No complete structured service report is assumed upstream.
Test native forms first. s2 counts unmatched items and manual entries; offline work uses current notes and later entry rather than free extraction.
s3 retains full report check and escalation. Approval binds the exact report and does not authorise equipment release.
unknowns: Existing mobile forms, field connectivity and duplicated entry share
research_questions: Does one service capture reduce later work-order rewriting after offline entry and all report checks?

already_counted.description: Manual report completion and exception descriptions in s2
Exact-version report check and deficiency notification in s3

incremental.description: Maintain local report choices and inspect synchronisation failures

approvals.approved_version: Exact asset/job, time, parts/materials, fault/deficiency descriptions, unusual occurrences and report revision; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Standalone task B=100, R=40+16+20=76; gross 24 minus 1.5 upkeep gives net 22.5. High needs current duplicate report entry; low covers offline and unusual cases consuming the benefit. Shared fact capture must be allocated once with repair-history recording.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study heating and cooling equipment specifications

steps.what: Find blueprints specifications and manufacturer recommendations for heating or cooling equipment components
Study component configuration and installation requirements against actual equipment conditions

tasks.design: Configure equipment-linked reference views in {DOCS} or the existing {OTHER} maintenance system. The mechanic checks applicability and studies original drawings and recommendations against the installed equipment; no generated answer replaces technical interpretation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applicable component references are scattered among versions and variants.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document links and metadata can narrow retrieval.
tasks.still_hard: Modified equipment and inconsistent component references.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a document does not describe the actual installation.
tasks.altitude: Less reference hunting; technical interpretation remains unchanged.

reach.learn: Which differences require revised drawings or specialist assessment

evidence.claim: Equipment-linked document retrieval is a plausible configuration; the proposed applicability checks and saving need local validation.

assumptions: Boundary is reference retrieval and study, excluding component installation and design authorisation.
Existing asset administration produces asset/model/configuration IDs and document control produces document revision/status through unchanged capture.
s1 retains selecting documents and checking applicability; missing metadata uses manual register lookup, with no new tagging assumed free.
s2 retains all technical interpretation and physical configuration checks.
Test native links/search first; existing automatic retrieval earns no new saving.
unknowns: Reference metadata and actual search burden
research_questions: Can native links reduce searching after confirming actual component identity and revision?

already_counted.description: Reference selection and applicability checks in s1

incremental.description: Inspect stale links and report reference mismatches

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=9+80=89; gross 11 minus 1 focal upkeep gives net 10. High needs existing reliable metadata; low covers manual lookup and configuration mismatch. Other-role reference upkeep is separate.
